subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as a first-run auth method, and what consent, scope, callback, token-storage, refresh, account-detection, billing, and fallback contract is acceptable?
rationale: Current code has reusable OAuth pieces, but turning them into one-click Anthropic onboarding changes credential handling and provider policy in ways automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Add Provider-Owned OAuth After Approval
options.body: Expose an additive Anthropic OAuth auth method through the Anthropic plugin after maintainers approve security, billing, docs, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Keep Explicit Auth Paths
options.body: Keep API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI as the supported Anthropic setup paths and improve copy or docs instead of adding browser OAuth now.

options.title: Prototype Behind Experimental UX
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth path that does not replace current Anthropic setup choices until live provider and security proof are strong.

recommendation.title: Add Provider-Owned OAuth After Approval
recommendation.body: Expose an additive Anthropic OAuth auth method through the Anthropic plugin after maintainers approve security, billing, docs, and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Anthropic auth-choice registration, docs, and auth-helper history point most strongly to steipete for the product/security boundary decision.
